title: Define the Purpose of the Area
subtitle: A space cannot be good at everything. Before you move a thing, give it one clear job in a single honest sentence.
hands_off_to: Part Three, Sort (Chapter 8, Sort: Remove What Does Not Belong)
audience: Readers who have chosen, audited, and photographed a space and are about to sort it. Busy home keepers and parents. New to applying the method.
core_promise: Decide what your space is actually for, in one written sentence, so that every keep-or-go decision in the sorting that follows becomes fast and easy.
emotional_purpose: Clarity and permission. Replace the vague guilt of a multi-purpose mess with one clear job, and give the reader permission to define a space for their real life rather than an ideal one.
practical_purpose: Establish purpose as the decision rule that comes before sorting, diagnose the everything-space, give the one-sentence Purpose Statement tool, and show how a clear purpose sets a space's limits and prevents re-cluttering.
primary_cta: Write your purpose sentence: name the one job your space exists to do, write it as 'this space is for ___, so that ___', keep it to one primary job, and match it to the people who actually live there. Read the chapter free in the online book.
secondary_cta: Read the chapter free online, then continue to Chapter 8 to begin the sorting.
keywords: how to organize a space with a purpose
hero_device: The Purpose Statement (a fill-in-the-blank sentence: 'This space is for one primary job, so that an outcome you actually want')
secondary_device: One Job Beats Five (a space asked to do five jobs is good at none; one clear job makes it good at that)
the_one_job_rule: A space cannot be good at everything. Give it one clear job, and at most one supporting job, and it will finally be good at that.

worked_example.purpose: This entryway is for getting everyone out the door fast and landing softly on the way back in, so that mornings start calm instead of frantic.
worked_example.primary_job: launch pad for leaving and arriving

definition: A space cannot be good at everything. Give it one clear job, and at most one supporting job, and it will finally be good at that. Everything that does not serve the job has a better home elsewhere.
one_idea_to_keep: A space cannot be good at everything. Decide its one job, in a single sentence, and you have just made every sorting decision that follows almost automatic.
key_motifs: match it to your real life, not an ideal
purpose sets the limits (a bouncer at the door)
the number, the picture, and the purpose complete the preparation
the friction meter GOAL crosshair gains a purpose flag (fully aimed)
